answer: In the agent economy a Sybil-resistant mechanism ties identity cost to a sparse attestation graph. Each new agent must obtain endorsements that form a trellis connecting it to an established vertex of bonded capital. Crossing the mesa of low-stake clones becomes expensive because forging many parallel paths requires locking real collateral at every hop, raising the attacker’s capital requirement linearly with the number of fake identities while honest agents reuse existing links.
